scenario.context: FreshBowl delivers meal kits weekly to 60,000 subscribers across Indian metros. Order size, skip rate and plan choice vary widely.

steps.task: Pick one segmentation basis, define 4 segments (criteria, size guess, key need), and choose one to prioritise.
hints: Use one basis only, such as motivation or behaviour.
Each segment should need something different from the product.

content.basis: Main reason for subscribing, checked against behaviour.

segments.name: Time-poor professionals
segments.criteria: 25 to 40, 2 to 3 meals a week, rarely skip

segments.name: Deal-driven trialists
segments.criteria: Join on promos, skip often, churn within 6 weeks

priority.name: Time-poor professionals
priority.reason: Large, low skip rate, high lifetime value and referrals.

reference.whyItWorks: One basis, mutually exclusive segments, and a priority backed by value.
commonMistakes: Mixing bases (age plus city plus diet)
Segments that need the same thing

scenario.context: LearnLoop is a language-learning app with 2M monthly users and 4% paid conversion. Some users learn daily for a month then quit; others do a short burst before a trip.

steps.task: Segment learners by goal and commitment into 4 segments and choose where to focus to raise paid conversion.
hints: Goal explains why they learn; commitment explains how long they stay.
Willingness to pay differs by goal.

content.basis: Goal (why they learn) and commitment (how long they stay).

segments.name: Trip-prep sprinters
segments.criteria: 10 to 30 day burst, want survival phrases
segments.need: Low lifetime value, buy short passes

segments.name: Career movers
segments.criteria: 3 to 5 sessions a week, want certificates
segments.need: Highest willingness to pay, need a structured path

segments.name: Heritage learners
segments.criteria: Learning a family language, slow and steady

segments.name: Streak hobbyists
segments.criteria: Casual daily use, motivated by games
segments.need: Low willingness to pay but high engagement

priority.name: Career movers
priority.reason: They convert and retain best; offer certificates and a study plan.

reference.whyItWorks: Segments link to different value and different product bets.
commonMistakes: Segmenting by age or country only

scenario.context: LedgerLite sells accounting software to small businesses and has 18,000 accounts. Support load is high, and two kinds of buyer appear: business owners, and accountants who run several client businesses.

steps.task: Segment by the job the software does and who the buyer is. Recommend a focus for the next 12 months and one risk.
hints: One accountant can bring many accounts.

content.basis: The job the software does and who the buyer is.

segments.name: Solo freelancers
segments.need: Simplicity; easy self-serve, low revenue per account

segments.name: Accountants managing many clients
segments.criteria: ~15% of accounts but each controls 10 to 40 client workspaces

priority.name: Accountants managing many clients
priority.reason: One win brings many workspaces and referrals.

content.risk: Multi-client features need heavy build, and the core self-serve base may be neglected; mitigate with a phased rollout.

reference.whyItWorks: Uses jobs and buyer, not just company size, and weighs channel leverage.
commonMistakes: Treating each account as one user
